summary: This note surveys architectural history from ancient wonders to contemporary sustainable design, organized by era: ancient, classical, religious, Renaissance/baroque, industrial, global contemporary, and sustainability. It pairs landmark structures like the Pyramids of Giza, Colosseum, Notre-Dame, Taj Mahal and Eiffel Tower with several dated events and projects from 2023 to 2025. It closes by stressing cultural preservation, with UNESCO World Heritage Sites central to protecting these structures.
one_line: A chronological tour of architectural landmarks from Gobekli Tepe to sustainable projects like The Lungs of Lagos, with notes on heritage preservation.
key_facts: Gobekli Tepe in modern-day Turkey has a temple complex dated to approximately 10,000 BCE, predating Stonehenge by 6,000 years.
The Pyramids of Giza were built around 2560 BCE as tombs for pharaohs and are aligned to the stars.
On the 21st of October 2023, archeologist Helena Zaras unearthed a previously unknown amphitheater in Athens, Greece, believed to date to around 350 BCE.
The Colosseum in Rome, built in 80 CE, could seat 50,000 spectators.
Notre-Dame de Paris, dating to the 12th century, had its spire lost in the fire of April 2019 and restored by 1st September 2023.
On the 3rd November 2023, the world celebrated the 400th anniversary of the completion of the Taj Mahal, built by Emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his late wife.
Filippo Brunelleschi's dome for the Florence Cathedral, completed in the 15th century, was an engineering marvel of its time.
On the 8th of September 2023, Dr. Alessandro Conti published a 20-year study on the construction techniques of St. Peter's Basilica in Vatican City.
The Eiffel Tower was constructed in 1887-1889 as a temporary exhibit for the 1889 World's Fair.
On the 14th of September 2023, Chicago commemorated the 130th anniversary of the Monadnock Building, a pivotal steel-frame skyscraper.
Zhang Yiling's Shanghai International Plaza, completed in September 2024, fuses traditional Chinese motifs with sustainable technologies.
The renewed Grand Egyptian Museum in Cairo, designed by Huda El-Sharkawy, was completed on September 17, 2025.
Jules Toure's 'The Lungs of Lagos' was inaugurated on October 15, 2023, using living walls and solar harvesting roofs and combining traditional Yoruba designs with modern sustainability.
